_why: A request document for `serverosctl ability resolve`, and deliberately a
MINIMAL one. The resolver takes eight inputs; this file supplies three and
names none of the other five.
That is the point. `abilities/resolver.py` records which of the eight it
could read (`inputs_seen`) and which it could not (`inputs_missing`),
because a confident AVAILABLE computed from whichever inputs happened to be
readable is the failure the kernel exists to prevent. A request that filled
in all eight would demonstrate the resolver agreeing with its own caller;
this one demonstrates it saying what it could not see.
Until now the resolver had no example request anywhere in the tree, so the
only callers were its own tests. §45's question — can THIS device do THIS
thing, now, and if not why not — could not be asked from the CLI by anybody
who had not first read resolver.py.
